entities.summary: James Reid was a Scottish trade union activist, orator, politician and journalist born in Govan, Glasgow. His role as spokesman and one of the leaders in the Upper Clyde Shipbuilders work-in between June 1971 and October 1972 attracted international recognition. He later served as Rector of the University of Glasgow and subsequently became a journalist and broadcaster. Formerly a member of the Communist Party of Great Britain, Reid was later a member of the Labour Party. He moved on to supporting the Scottish Socialist Party in the late 1990s, then joined the Scottish National Party in 2005 and gave his full support to the idea of Scottish independence.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a leader of the Upper Clyde Shipbuilders work-in, Reid's actions influenced UK labor laws and inspired similar industrial disputes worldwide. His involvement in Scottish politics further solidified his legacy as a champion of workers' rights.
